precedent.note: The Constitutional Court treats stare decisis as part of the rule of law: precedent binds lower courts, and courts of final jurisdiction are bound by their own decisions unless clearly wrong. Only the ratio decidendi binds, not obiter dicta.

courts.name: Constitutional Court
courts.note: S. 167(3)(a): highest court of the Republic; may decide constitutional matters and, with leave, any other arguable point of law of general public importance. Before the Constitution Seventeenth Amendment Act of 2012 it was highest only in constitutional matters; that Act came into operation on 23 August 2013 (Proc. R. 35 of 2013).

courts.name: Supreme Court of Appeal
courts.note: S. 168(3): decides appeals in any matter from the High Court or a court of similar status, except labour or competition matters to the extent an Act of Parliament provides. Further appeal to the Constitutional Court with its leave (s. 167(3)(b), 167(6)(b)).

courts.name: High Court of South Africa
courts.note: A single High Court made up of Divisions (s. 169; Superior Courts Act s. 6(1)), created by the Seventeenth Amendment and the Superior Courts Act, both in force 23 August 2013; the former separate High Courts became seats of Divisions (SCA Act s. 50(1)). Appeals from a Division at first instance go, with leave, to the SCA or (single judge) to a full court of the same Division; appeals decided by a Division on appeal go to the SCA with special leave (SCA Act s. 16(1)(a)-(b)). Direct appeal to the Constitutional Court with its leave (s. 167(6)(b)).

courts.name: Magistrates' Courts
courts.note: District courts and regional-division courts established under Magistrates' Courts Act s. 2(1)(f)-(g). Civil appeals lie to the High Court Division having jurisdiction (MCA s. 83, read with SCA Act s. 53(b)); criminal appeals from a lower court lie, with leave, to the High Court having jurisdiction (CPA s. 309(1)(a)). Appeals to the Land Court lie where land-related legislation confers that jurisdiction (Land Court Act s. 17(1)). S. 170: courts below the High Court may not rule on the constitutionality of legislation or presidential conduct. A High Court Division's decisions bind the magistrates' courts within that Division's area only. No relation records it: a relation of the High Court to the magistrates' courts would cover every Division and every area.

courts.name: Labour Court
courts.note: Superior court with authority equal to a provincial division of the High Court in matters under its jurisdiction (LRA s. 151(2)). Appeals against its final judgments and orders go, with leave, to the Labour Appeal Court (ss. 166, 173(1)(a)).

courts.name: Labour Appeal Court
courts.note: Final court of appeal for Labour Court judgments in matters within that court's exclusive jurisdiction, with standing equal to the SCA in its own matters (LRA s. 167(2)-(3)). S. 183 bars appeals from it, subject to the Constitution; s. 168(3)(a) of the Constitution lets an Act exclude labour matters from the SCA, and s. 167(6)(b) allows a direct appeal to the Constitutional Court with leave.

courts.name: Land Claims Court
courts.note: Established by Restitution of Land Rights Act s. 22. Appeals, with leave, heard by the SCA (s. 37(1)-(2), as substituted in 1996 and amended in 1997); s. 37(9) preserves a direct appeal to the Constitutional Court. Chapter III (the court's provisions) was deleted by Land Court Act Schedule item 4, in force 5 April 2024; pending matters pass to the Land Court (Land Court Act s. 35(1)(b)).

courts.name: Land Court
courts.note: Superior court with standing equal to a Division of the High Court in its matters (Land Court Act s. 3(2)(a)). Appeals from a single judge go, with leave, to the SCA or a full court of the Land Court; from a full court on appeal, to the SCA with special leave (s. 31(1)), subject to the Constitution (direct appeal to the Constitutional Court, Constitution s. 167(6)(b)). Act in force 5 April 2024 except s. 37 and Schedule items 1, 2, 3, 6 and 7.

courts.name: Competition Appeal Court
courts.note: Court under s. 166(e) of the Constitution with status similar to a High Court (Competition Act s. 36(1)(a)). Final in matters within its exclusive jurisdiction; on jurisdictional and constitutional questions (s. 62(2)) appeal lies to the Constitutional Court with its leave (ss. 62(4), 63(2) as amended by Act 18 of 2018, in force 12 July 2019). Before that date s. 62(4) also allowed appeals to the SCA.

courts.name: Competition Tribunal
courts.note: Tribunal of record with national jurisdiction (Competition Act s. 26(1)). Its decisions may be appealed to, or reviewed by, the Competition Appeal Court (ss. 37(1), 61(1)).

courts.name: Electoral Court
courts.note: Established with the status of the Supreme Court (Electoral Commission Act s. 18), a reference now read as the High Court (SCA Act s. 53(b)). Electoral Act s. 96(1) says its decisions on electoral disputes and Code complaints are not subject to appeal or review; the Constitutional Court nonetheless granted leave for a direct appeal from it on a constitutional issue in [2024] ZACC 6, paras 28-30.

rests_on.quote: If it is not clearly wrong, this Court and all others are bound by it: stare decisis.
Right or wrong, courts lower in the hierarchy are bound by it.
Now that this Court is the highest court on all matters, the statement applies to all its decisions.

relations.note: Para 57: a Constitutional Court ratio that is not clearly wrong binds that Court and all other courts. Para 58: now that it is highest court in all matters, this applies to all its decisions, not only constitutional ones.

rests_on.quote: The doctrine of precedent not only binds lower courts but also binds courts of final jurisdiction to their own decisions. These courts can depart from a previous decision of their own only when satisfied that that decision is clearly wrong.
If it is clearly wrong but not obiter, this Court – and it alone – is at liberty to depart from it.

relations.note: Courts of final jurisdiction are bound by their own decisions and may depart only when satisfied the earlier decision is clearly wrong; only the Constitutional Court may depart from its own clearly wrong ratio.

rests_on.provision: para 29, quoting S v Walters, paras 60-61
rests_on.quote: High Courts are obliged to follow legal interpretations of the Supreme Court of Appeal, whether they relate to constitutional issues or to other issues, and remain so obliged unless and until the Supreme Court of Appeal itself decides otherwise or this Court does so in respect of a constitutional issue.

relations.note: Both judgments quote S v Walters paras 60-61: High Courts must follow the SCA's legal interpretations, constitutional or otherwise, until the SCA itself or the Constitutional Court decides otherwise.

rests_on.provision: The Court's position in the justice system
rests_on.quote: Decisions of the Supreme Court of Appeal are binding on all lesser courts and the decisions of the High Courts (which used to be known as the Supreme Courts) are binding on Magistrates' Courts within their areas.

relations.note: The Constitutional Court's website states that SCA decisions bind all lesser courts.

rests_on.quote: A judgment of the Labour Appeal Court is binding on the Labour Court.

relations.note: LRA s. 182: a judgment of the Labour Appeal Court binds the Labour Court.
